paper_metadata.title: Quantum synergy in peptide folding: A comparative study of CVaR-variational quantum eigensolver and molecular dynamics simulation

summary: The paper compares CVaR-VQE against molecular dynamics for 50 seven-residue peptides on a coarse-grained tetrahedral lattice. The VQE study uses 9 qubits, 500,000 shots per iteration, and 100 iterations per peptide on an Amazon Braket local/statevector simulator; the MD baseline reports mean energy dropping from 9.58 kcal/mol at native state to 2.68 kcal/mol at 50 ns, with 36/50 peptides reaching ground state within 50 ns.

experiments.description: CVaR-VQE peptide folding study on 50 seven-residue peptides using a coarse-grained tetrahedral lattice model, compared against molecular dynamics as a classical baseline.

algorithm.ansatz: parameterized quantum circuit with Hadamard, conditional rotational gates, and CNOT gates; enhanced number of conditional rotational gates compared with prior work
algorithm.optimizer: surrogateopt (Global Optimization Toolbox); genetic method mentioned in prior work
algorithm.parameter_initialization: rotation angles optimized via surrogateopt; prior work used genetic method

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 7 qubits encode the 7 amino-acid configuration; 2 additional qubits encode interactions (including one helper qubit not measured); dense encoding used to reduce qubit count
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize exact Hamiltonian energy of coarse-grained peptide fold; CVaR objective averages the lower-energy tail of sampled bitstrings
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Penalty terms enforce valid turns, prevent backtracking/overlap, and impose chirality; valid initialization and gate operations conserve the number of 1s in each 4-qubit turn block when possible
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Exact Hamiltonian with nearest-neighbor interaction terms and penalty terms for invalid geometries/chirality

problem_instance.description: Protein folding for intrinsically disordered peptide regions; 50 randomly selected 7-residue peptides from the 7 most disorder-promoting amino acids

dataset_specification.description: 50 sequences selected from 5040 possible permutations of 7 residues; residues chosen from D, H, Q, K, S, E, P

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Sequences imported into Maestro/Schrodinger 3D builder for MD baseline; for quantum model, coarse-grained lattice mapping and dense encoding applied
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Each peptide evaluated with 100 VQE iterations and 500,000 shots per iteration; results compared against MD baseline and summarized with statistical analysis (two-tailed t-test, R-squared reported)

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Peptide sequences built in Maestro/Schrodinger; protein preparation with Epik and OPLS3e for MD baseline
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Exact Hamiltonian evaluated on sampled bitstrings; probabilities sorted by energy and CVaR tail expectation computed

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: energy optimization over 100 iterations; example peptides reported stability after 42 and 63 iterations

speedup_claims.conditions: The paper makes an empirical comparison of folding/energy outcomes and sampling efficiency, not a formal runtime speedup claim.
speedup_claims.caveats: No asymptotic or wall-clock speedup is reported for the quantum method; the paper emphasizes better sampling/global optimization rather than faster execution.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: No demonstrated quantum resource advantage; the experiment uses a local statevector simulator with 9 logical qubits and 500,000 shots per iteration.
limiting_factors: Classical baseline is MD, not a classical optimizer for the same quantum objective
Problem size is small (50 peptides, 7 residues each)
Reported results are empirical and do not establish quantum advantage

notes: Hardware inferred as simulator_statevector because the paper explicitly states use of Amazon Braket local simulator and SVI state vector simulator, with no real QPU device named.
num_qubits reported from text stating 7 configuration qubits plus 2 interaction qubits (9 total).
Circuit depth not explicitly reported; only circuit structure and gate types are described, so null was used.
Speedup order is not characterized asymptotically; the paper presents an empirical comparison to MD, not a proven quantum speedup.

The paper compares CVaR-VQE against molecular dynamics and reports better ground-state energy outcomes for VQE on 49/50 peptides, but this is not a Hoefler-style practical quantum advantage demonstration.
The computation is performed on a simulator, so no hardware advantage is shown.

experiments.description: Classical molecular dynamics (MD) baseline for the same 50 seven-residue peptides, used as the comparison method against CVaR-VQE.
key_results: Mean MD energy decreased from 9.58 kcal/mol at native state to 2.68 kcal/mol at 50 ns.
Ground state reached by 36/50 peptides within 50 ns; 14/50 did not reach ground state.
Ground state timing distribution: 26 peptides at 50 ns, 6 at 40 ns, 9 at 30 ns, 8 at 20 ns, 1 at 10 ns.
Best observed simulation window for ground state was 40-50 ns, with approximate energy around 4 kcal/mol.
